---
title: "Shell Performance"
description: "Repeatable production benchmark for theme switching, app-to-app navigation, cold loads and shared chunk reuse across tuturuuu.com/<app>, with the measured baseline."
updatedAt: "2026-11-25"
---

Every app is served from one origin (`tuturuuu.com/<app>`) through the apex
gateway. Theme changes and app switches should feel instant: the theme is a
class swap with no request, and the shared shell (sidebar, top bar, account
menu) stays stable between apps. This page holds the benchmark that checks
this and the numbers each optimization is measured against.

## Running the benchmark

The benchmark is read-only. It signs in as a QA user and never writes data,
apart from closing first-run dialogs in that QA user's own workspace.

```bash
# 1. A disposable signed-in session (Pro staff QA user, 72h max).
ttr qa users create --count 1 --tier pro --staff --workspace \
  --purpose perf-shell-bench --ttl 24h --json
ttr qa users session <user-id> --origin https://tuturuuu.com \
  --format storage-state --out state.json

# 2. Run (3 samples per measurement; the median is reported).
node apps/web/e2e/perf/shell-benchmark.mjs state.json out.json \
  https://tuturuuu.com 3
```

`BENCH_APPS` (cold loads) and `BENCH_SWITCH` (the app-switch sequence)
override the default app lists. Point the origin at a staged 0% Worker
version or a local production build to measure a change before promotion. Do
not run the benchmark against a dev server, because dev bundles skew every
number.

The benchmark measures:

| Area | How |
| --- | --- |
| Theme toggle | Real account-menu path (Theme → Dark/Light, keyboard-activated). Click-to-class time, Event Timing interaction latency, requests fired, layout shift, DOM churn, and the number of CSS transitions the swap starts plus how long they take to settle. |
| App-to-app switch | One warm browser context visits each app in turn. Reports TTFB, FCP, LCP, CLS, JS/CSS KB downloaded and the `Cache-Control` header on the HTML document. |
| Cold load | A fresh context per sample (empty HTTP cache). |
| Chunk reuse | SHA-256 of every script body across apps: identical content under the same URL (reused), identical content under different URLs (wasted downloads), and app-unique bytes. |
| Back/forward cache | CDP `Page.backForwardCacheNotUsed` reasons after a history back. Headless Chromium also reports `BackForwardCacheDisabledByCommandLine`; the app-caused reasons are the other ones. |

## Baseline (2026-11-25, production)

Chromium headless, 1440×900, from Vietnam, signed in as a Pro staff QA user.
These are medians of 3 samples. Live production varies by about ±30%, so
compare a change with a run taken at the same time and place.

### Theme toggle

| App | Click → class | Interaction (INP) | Requests | CLS | CSS transitions started | Visual settle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mail | 7 ms | 24 ms | 0 | 0 | 93 | 500 ms |
| Calendar | 24 ms | 64 ms | 0 | 0 | 1406 | 300 ms |
| Tasks | 12 ms | 32 ms | 0 | 0 | 224 | 500 ms |
| Finance | 4 ms | 24 ms | 0 | 0 | 316 | 500 ms |
| Web dashboard | 2-4 ms | n/a | 0 | 0 | 350 | 500 ms |

The class swap itself was already cheap. It caused no request, no reload, no
React remount and no layout shift. The theme also already follows the user
across apps, because every app on the shared origin reads the same `theme`
localStorage key and next-themes syncs other tabs through the `storage` event.
The switch still looked slow, because every element with `transition-colors`
or `transition-all` animated to the new palette for 300-500 ms.

next-themes' `disableTransitionOnChange` does not fix this in Chromium. It
calls `getComputedStyle(document.body)` without reading a property, which does
not flush styles, so transitions still start. Injecting that exact sequence on
production left all 92-1403 transitions running.

### App-to-app switch (warm context)

| Step | TTFB | FCP | LCP | JS downloaded | Total downloaded |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → Mail (first) | 1512 ms | 2400 ms | 4600 ms | 688 KB | 813 KB |
| → Calendar | 2345 ms | 2472 ms | 4896 ms | 2289 KB | 2449 KB |
| → Tasks | 5836 ms | 8044 ms | 8044 ms | 2612 KB | 2765 KB |
| → Drive (web) | 51 ms | 1128 ms | 1128 ms | 411 KB | 1214 KB |
| → Finance | 2473 ms | 2876 ms | 2876 ms | 1346 KB | 1636 KB |
| → Mail (revisit) | 1602 ms | 1636 ms | 2548 ms | 0 KB | 22 KB |
| → Calendar (revisit) | 2770 ms | 2916 ms | 3180 ms | 0 KB | 52 KB |
| → Tasks (revisit) | 6213 ms | 6340 ms | 6340 ms | 13 KB | 60 KB |

CLS was 0 for every navigation. Every switch is a full document navigation.
None of the pages has Speculation Rules, and every HTML response is
`Cache-Control: private, no-store`, which also blocks the back/forward cache
(`MainResourceHasCacheControlNoStore`,
`JsNetworkRequestReceivedCacheControlNoStoreResource`).

| App | TTFB | FCP | LCP | JS requests | JS KB | Total KB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mail | 1422 ms | 1616 ms | 2884 ms | 21 | 689 | 814 |
| Calendar | 2053 ms | 2972 ms | 4368 ms | 28 | 2315 | 2479 |
| Tasks | 5099 ms | 5328 ms | 5328 ms | 20 | 2634 | 2800 |
| Finance | 3317 ms | 3636 ms | 3636 ms | 290 | 1372 | 1670 |
| Meet | 1472 ms | 1728 ms | 1728 ms | 87 | 560 | 833 |
| Drive (web) | 187 ms | 1416 ms | 1416 ms | 88 | 438 | 1243 |
| Chat (web) | 167 ms | 1216 ms | 1216 ms | 88 | 437 | 1243 |
| Web dashboard | 164 ms | 1380 ms | 1596 ms | 324 | 2463 | 3019 |

### Chunk reuse across apps

This was measured over 610 distinct scripts from the eight cold loads.

- About 2.5 MB is identical content under the same URL. That is the
  `/_f/dashboard` chunks shared by the web-hosted surfaces (dashboard, Drive,
  Chat).
- Only 106 KB is identical content under different URLs. Each satellite
  (`/mail/assets`, `/calendar/assets`, `/tasks/assets`, `/finance/assets`,
  `/meet/assets`) bundles its own copy of React, `@tuturuuu/ui` and vendor
  code, with different chunk boundaries and hashes. Serving the same files
  from one shared path does not fix this on its own. The satellites first need
  one shared build of the common packages.
- About 32 MB is app-unique, so a user's first visit to each satellite
  re-downloads 0.7-2.6 MB of JS.

## Ranked opportunities

1. **Server time (TTFB 1.4-6.2 s on satellites, including revisits).** This is
   the largest cost of every app switch. Tasks spends about 5-6 s before the
   first byte. Profile the per-request session and workspace resolution and the
   Supabase round trips in the satellite Workers. Cache the shell data (user,
   workspaces, apps list) with stale-while-revalidate.
2. **Per-app vendor and UI bundles (0.7-2.6 MB per first visit).** Share one
   build of React and `@tuturuuu/ui` across satellites behind one immutable
   path, or prefetch the next app's entry chunks.
3. **Cross-app navigation.** Add Speculation Rules (`prefetch`, then
   `prerender` for sidebar app links) and cross-document View Transitions for
   the shell. Restore back/forward cache eligibility where `no-store` is not
   needed for safety.
4. **Theme swap animation (300-500 ms).** Fixed by `InstantThemeSwap` below.

## Theme switching contract

Every app's theme provider spreads `tuturuuuThemeProviderProps` from
`@tuturuuu/ui/custom/theme-provider-preset` and renders
`<InstantThemeSwap nonce={nonce} />` from `@tuturuuu/ui/custom/instant-theme-swap`
inside it. This covers the shared satellite providers (`providers.tsx`,
`public-providers.tsx`), web, workspace, Mail, Calendar, Tasks, Meet,
Mastermind, Chat, Contacts, Forms, Learn, Mind, Nova, Pay, Teach, Colab and
the native apps shell.

The guard watches the light/dark class on `<html>` and acts before the next
frame, whether the change comes from the menu, another tab or the OS
preference. It flushes styles once while transitions are disabled, so the new
colors become the starting values and nothing animates. Per the CSS
Transitions spec, the flush also cancels any transition already in flight,
such as a sidebar collapse, which jumps to its end state at the moment of the
switch. The injected rule carries the request CSP nonce.

The guard was measured by injecting it into the current production pages (the
numbers for the shipped build follow once it deploys):

| App | Running transitions (before → after) | Visual settle (before → after) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mail | 92 → 0 | 500 ms → 9 ms |
| Calendar | 1403 → 0 | 300 ms → 20 ms |
| Tasks | 206 → 0 | 500 ms → 16 ms |
| Finance | 309 → 0 | 500 ms → 10 ms |
| Web dashboard | 350 → 0 | 500 ms → 12 ms |

Regression coverage:

- `apps/web/e2e/theme-switch.noauth.spec.ts` drives the swap through the
  cross-tab `storage` path. It asserts no main-frame document request, CLS 0,
  no color transitions, and the class applied within 250 ms of the event
  landing. It is read-only. The web e2e global setup accepts only local
  origins, so to check a deployed origin (production or a 0% Worker version),
  run the file with a Playwright config that drops `globalSetup` and sets
  `BASE_URL`. Subframes such as the Turnstile widget may re-theme themselves
  and are excluded.
- `packages/ui/src/components/ui/custom/instant-theme-swap.test.tsx` and
  `theme-provider-preset.test.tsx` pin the guard and the shared options.

A new app shell must use the preset and render the guard. Do not set
`disableTransitionOnChange` as a substitute.
